summary.intent: Execute all 4 plans in Phase 59 (FUSE IPNS verify/publish hardening and cleanup) using wave-based execution, and investigate a staging storage quota anomaly for a specific user while the final plan ran.
summary.outcome: Waves 1–3 (plans 59-01, 59-02, 59-03) completed and verified with 96 tests passing; Wave 4 (59-04) was still running at transcript end. The staging quota investigation identified 239 pinned CIDs totaling 442MB concentrated in 9 large blobs from March 30–April 2, with the unpin pipeline suspected as the root cause.

repo: Root `npm test` runs `pnpm --parallel -r run test` (full monorepo) — for Rust-only phases, scope the post-merge gate to `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` to avoid RAM exhaustion.

CI does not run clippy at all; no `.github/workflows/` file references it. The plans' 'clippy -D warnings exits 0' acceptance criterion is unachievable because the pre-existing `cipherbox-crypto` dependency fails first.
24 pre-existing clippy warnings exist in the fuse crate (8 vendored `fuse_*` ABI structs, the rest `too_many_arguments`/`div_ceil`/`Default impl`); none were introduced by phase 59.

Legacy IPNS records: 23/43 rows (53%) on staging have `signed_record IS NULL`, predating the signing convention that landed 2026-04-04 (#448). The legacy verify path fires on the majority of current staging data.
2 staging rows have partial sig fields (`signed_record` present, `public_key` NULL) — treated as a downgrade vector in verify code, distinct from true-legacy.

FUSE embeds IPNS sequence `0` on first publish; the TS SDK and API assume `1`. This skew is tolerated by a temporary allowance in `verify.rs` (`resp_seq==1 && embedded_seq==0`) being removed in 59-04.

Quota accounting is `SUM(pinned_cids.size_bytes)` per user, computed live. The only decrement path is an explicit `/ipfs/unpin` — the client delete→bin→empty-bin pipeline never triggers unpin, causing quota to accumulate indefinitely.
The 442MB quota anomaly is concentrated: 9 CIDs ≥1MB account for 439MB, all pinned March 30–April 2 (early test vaults, never re-published or unpinned).

code.finding: Write site for `VerifiedResolve::signature_verified` field — removed in 59-03 (E.1 dead-field removal)
Second write site for the now-removed `VerifiedResolve::signature_verified` field

Pre-existing `Default impl` clippy lint; file also embeds IPNS sequence `0` on first publish (changed to `1` in 59-04)

workflow: Worktree isolation is only justified for concurrent parallel plan execution — single-plan waves should run sequentially on the main branch to avoid the merge dance, node_modules problems, and SUMMARY.md loss risk.
When a worktree subagent needs `node_modules`, it must run `pnpm i` to initialize its own copy; symlinking back to the parent checkout is wrong and should never be done.

GSD failure-mode #2070: a subagent may complete all code work and write `SUMMARY.md` but then get interrupted (e.g., 522) before committing it. Rescue: commit the file directly inside the worktree before running any cleanup.
The `cleanup-wave` helper requires a valid `--manifest` path; a `mktemp` template collision can leave the variable empty and fail the merge silently — always verify the manifest path before invoking.
The state tracking helper may print `commit_failed` as a false negative while the commit actually succeeds — do not retry based on that message alone.
Piping SQL to `docker exec` via `-c` flag causes nested quoting failures; use `-i` with stdin redirection (`docker exec -i container psql ... <<< 'SQL'`) instead.

friction: Two Cloudflare 522 errors mid-session: one interrupted the Wave 1 subagent after all code work was done (SUMMARY.md not yet committed), one hit during the cleanup-wave merge attempt.
Wave 1 ran unnecessarily in a worktree (sequential phase, one plan per wave — zero parallelism to isolate), causing avoidable merge/cleanup overhead.
Wave 1 subagent created a `node_modules` symlink back to the parent repo as a husky/lint-staged workaround in the isolated worktree — required manual cleanup before merge.
`mktemp` template collision left the cleanup-wave `--manifest` variable empty on the first merge attempt, causing a silent failure requiring a retry with a fixed path.
Post-merge clippy gate produced confusing output because `cipherbox-crypto` dependency errors intermixed with fuse crate findings, requiring a `--no-deps` invocation to isolate fuse-specific results.
Nested SQL quoting via `docker exec -c` broke on the first staging DB query attempt.
open_items: Wave 4 (59-04) was still executing at transcript end — sequence `0→1` unification in `publish.rs`/`replay.rs` and strict `embedded_seq == resp_seq` enforcement in `verify.rs`.
Phase 59 completion sequence not yet run: TDD RED→GREEN gate check, code review, regression gate, phase-goal verifier.
Staging quota leak root cause not fully confirmed — `pending_unpins` queue and `folder_ipns` activity check for the affected user was initiated but results not shown.
Production legacy-record ratio unknown — only staging was queried (23/43 legacy); production may differ and a prod psql path was not available.
Plans' 'clippy `-D warnings` exits 0' acceptance criterion is unachievable as written (crypto dep fails first) — needs a note to the phase verifier to scope to `--no-deps`.
D.1 TODO (D-01a): `journal_entry` parameter retained in `publish_with_cas_retry` with a deferred TODO — dead param left in place intentionally for a later phase.
The 2 partial-field staging rows (`signed_record` present, `public_key` NULL) are an edge case neither cleanly legacy nor modern — worth a targeted investigation/backfill.
Phase 60 integration: 59-04's sequence unification is documented as 'bridging to Phase 60' — downstream compatibility needs verification.
